title: An oversized image scaled down by CSS vs one authored at display size
variable: 352x256 texture scaled to 88x64 vs a native 88x64 texture
claim: Antipattern #21 from web-performance-antipatterns-50.md: 'oversized images scaled down in CSS - decode + sample cost for pixels never shown.' Gameface adds a memory dimension the web list omits: RAG 15-tooling.md 'Tracking Texture Thrashing with Memory Counters' treats GPU texture allocation as a budget to watch. A 4x oversized texture occupies 16x the GPU memory of the one actually needed, whatever it costs per frame.
result: NOT CONFIRMED for per-frame cost. No reliable difference at any count from sampling a 352x256 texture down to 88x64 versus using a native 88x64 texture. IMPORTANT LIMIT: every tile shares one texture, so this row measures per-frame sampling only. The 4x asset still occupies 16x the GPU memory, which RAG 15-tooling.md treats as a budget to watch and which this case does not measure. A null here is not a licence to ship oversized art.
notes: Applicability gate: DIRECT. url() was verified manually against the Player (its 'unsupported' inventory entry is a probe skip, not a finding) and background-size is fully supported. Rule 1: one variable, the source texture's resolution. Rule 2: identical DOM and geometry; both variants declare the same background-size: 88px 64px so the rendered result is the same 88x64 picture in both. Rule 3: identical JS, byte-for-byte. Rule 4 EXCEPTION: the two variants load different assets - that IS the variable. Both are generated by tools/make-baked-images.js from the SAME normalised drawing function at 1x and 4x, so they are the same artwork at two resolutions rather than two different pictures, which is what keeps the comparison about resolution alone. Rule 5: 300 tiles occupy 1852x1032 inside 1920x1080. Rule 6: the shared root-nudge damage driver, identical in both. Rule 7: no randomness. Rule 8: counts 30/100/300. Rule 9: plain HTML/CSS/JS. Rule 10: expected axis is GPU - sampling a 4x texture down to the same target should be the sampler's problem, not layout's. NOTE: every tile shares one texture, so this row measures per-frame sampling cost, not the one-off decode or the memory footprint. A null result here would NOT clear oversized art of the memory charge.
